findings.title: Critical: Command Injection via subprocess.run with shell=True
findings.impact: Arbitrary code execution with application privileges
findings.evidence: The summarize_and_run() function directly executes model output as a shell command via subprocess.run(model_output, shell=True, capture_output=True, text=True).stdout. Any malicious shell commands generated by the LLM will be executed with full shell interpretation.
findings.recommendation: Remove shell=True parameter and use subprocess.run() with shell=False and argument array. Alternatively, eliminate direct code execution entirely and use a whitelist of allowed commands. Add input validation, sanitization, and audit logging. Run with least privilege.

findings.title: Critical: Authorization Bypass in Tool Dispatcher
findings.impact: Unauthorized refunds and account access to arbitrary customer accounts
findings.evidence: The run_tool() function accepts tool requests without any authorization validation. It processes refund and lookup requests directly from model decision without checking if the caller is authorized. The session parameter is accepted but never used.
findings.recommendation: Always validate caller authorization from session parameter. Enforce account-scoped operations: only allow actions on session['authenticated_account_id']. Add audit logging of all tool invocations. Implement rate limiting and anomaly detection. Consider removing refund capability entirely.

findings.title: Critical: Hardcoded API Key Exposure
findings.impact: Unauthorized access to Acme billing system, ability to issue refunds and modify accounts
findings.evidence: The billing service API key 'sk-acme-1f4d8e2b9c7a6d5e4f3b2a1c0d9e8f7a' is hardcoded directly in configuration file. This key can be extracted via repository inspection, process environment inspection, configuration file backups, or dependency supply chain.
findings.recommendation: Immediately rotate the exposed API key. Load secrets from environment variables only, never from configuration files. Use secrets management system (Vault, AWS Secrets Manager, Azure Key Vault). Remove all secrets from repository history using BFG repo-cleaner or git-filter-branch. Implement secrets scanning in CI/CD pipeline.

findings.title: High: RAG Poisoning via Unvalidated Ticket Ingestion
findings.impact: Malicious customer tickets can influence model behavior for all subsequent interactions
findings.evidence: The ingest_ticket() function indexes customer-supplied ticket body without validation: index.add_texts([ticket['body']]). An attacker can submit tickets containing prompt injection instructions that will be indexed and later retrieved as context for the LLM.
findings.recommendation: Validate and sanitize all ticket content before indexing. Add explicit markers for untrusted data. Use separate isolated index for customer-submitted data. Implement content filtering to detect injection attempts. Monitor retrieve results for suspicious patterns. Add user feedback loop to identify and remove poisoned documents.

findings.title: High: Prompt Injection via Unvalidated Retrieved Documents
findings.impact: Attacker can craft documents that influence model behavior through retrieved context
findings.evidence: The build_prompt_marked() function includes document metadata (origin, trust) directly in prompts without verifying authenticity. An attacker can create documents with false origin/trust values to appear legitimate and include hidden instructions marked as trusted.
findings.recommendation: Never trust source/trust metadata - always validate from authoritative source. Implement strict document validation before retrieval. Use cryptographic signatures for important documents. Add explicit [UNTRUSTED] markers to all customer-sourced content. Implement per-document access controls. Use prompt armor/structured prompting to isolate instruction from data.

findings.title: High: Unsafe Memory Persistence - Model Output Storage Without Validation
findings.impact: Model-generated payload persists in memory and influences future conversations
findings.evidence: The remember_from_reply() function stores model output unvalidated: data.setdefault('notes', []).append(reply). An attacker can craft prompts that cause the model to generate instructions which are then stored and retrieved in future conversations, creating persistent compromise.
findings.recommendation: Never store model output in persistent memory directly. Only store structured, validated metadata. Implement content filtering before storage. Use immutable append-only log with integrity verification. Add cryptographic signatures. Implement access controls on memory file. Monitor for suspicious patterns. Add version/timestamp audit trail.

findings.title: Medium: Unsafe Dependency Resolution and Configuration
findings.impact: Dependency confusion attacks or installation of unexpected versions of MCP servers
findings.evidence: MCP configuration uses unpinned version '@acme/billing-mcp@latest' with auto-approval flag '-y'. Also uses unset environment variable substitution. No integrity verification or version pinning. npx downloads from npm without cached verification.
findings.recommendation: Always pin exact version numbers (e.g., @acme/billing-mcp@1.2.3). Remove '-y' flag to require explicit approval. Use package-lock.json with integrity hashes. Require environment variables to be set at startup. Use npm ci instead of npm install. Implement SBOM for supply chain security. Monitor for unexpected version changes.
